title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Profit is an opinion formed on the income statement; cash conversion and debt-to-fixed-asset discipline are facts audited on the balance sheet.
epigraph.author: Forensic accounting maxim

web_blocks.html: From FY21 through FY26 (and TTM to Sep 2026), SEDEMAC compounded rapidly. Revenue grew from ₹240 Cr in FY21 to ₹1,058 Cr in FY26 (34.5% 5Y CAGR) and ₹1,265 Cr TTM [1]. Net profit rose from ₹7 Cr to ₹104 Cr in FY26 (69.4% 5Y CAGR) and ₹129 Cr TTM [1]. Operating margins expanded from 10–12% (FY21–FY23) to 20% in FY26, before PCB and chip inflation trimmed OPM to 19% in Q1–Q2 FY27 [1, 5]. Crucially, headline H1 FY27 net profit growth was flattered by a sharp effective tax-rate drop: Screener's quarterly tax rate fell from 43% (Q1 FY26) and 33% (Q2 FY26; 31% full-year FY26) to 19% (Q1 FY27) and 22% (Q2 FY27) following the switch to India's new tax regime [1, 39]. Consequently, Q2 FY27 reported PAT rose +30.0% YoY (₹30 Cr to ₹39 Cr) even though Q2 PBT grew only +13.3% YoY (₹45 Cr to ₹51 Cr), and H1 FY27 PAT rose +53.2% YoY (₹47 Cr to ₹72 Cr) versus +22.7% YoY PBT growth (₹75 Cr to ₹92 Cr) [1].

web_blocks.caption: SEDEMAC Consolidated Profit & Loss Trajectory (Mar 2021 – TTM Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Revenue scaled 5.3x from FY21 (₹240 Cr) to TTM (₹1,265 Cr) with operating leverage lifting OPM from 10% (FY22) to 19–20% (FY26–TTM), though H1 FY27 PAT (+53.2% YoY) outpaced PBT (+22.7% YoY) due to the tax-rate drop to 19%–22% [1].

web_blocks.html: The most urgent forensic item sits on the September 2026 Balance Sheet [1]. In six months, total Borrowings jumped nearly 5x from ₹72 Cr to ₹352 Cr (+₹280 Cr) [1]. Fixed Assets doubled from ₹253 Cr to ₹518 Cr (+₹265 Cr), while CWIP moved to ₹63 Cr [1]. Footnotes split those aggregates cleanly. Financial debt rose nearly 5x from ₹50.63 Cr to ₹245.64 Cr. Short-term debt surged 7.4x from ₹20.75 Cr to ₹153.19 Cr. Ind AS 116 lease liabilities reached ₹106.47 Cr, matched by ₹144.16 Cr of Right-of-Use assets for MF3 Chakan. Q2 interest cost jumped to ₹6 Cr [1]. Three causes drove this: (1) the March 2026 IPO was a 100% OFS with ₹0 fresh cash; (2) MF3 and MF5 capex/leases [5]; and (3) working capital jumped to ~₹258 Cr as receivables rose 58.7% (₹212.16 Cr) and inventory rose 52.8% (₹287.81 Cr) [5].

web_blocks.caption: SEDEMAC Consolidated Balance Sheet Forensics (Mar 2021 – Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Sep 2026 Borrowings (₹352 Cr) split into ₹245.64 Cr financial debt (₹153.19 Cr current) + ₹106.47 Cr Ind AS 116 lease liabilities (matched by ₹144.16 Cr ROU assets) following a 100% OFS IPO [1, 5].

web_blocks.html: A second forensic flag is negative H1 FY27 cash conversion, plus DSO stretch and interest capitalization [1]. In FY26, CFO (₹128 Cr) covered 123% of PAT (₹104 Cr), though ₹175 Cr of capex pushed FCF to -₹47 Cr [1]. In H1 FY27, CFO flipped to -₹20.38 Cr (vs +₹120.73 Cr in H1 FY26) [1, 5]. SEDEMAC absorbed ₹99.50 Cr of inventory and ₹78.44 Cr of receivables while shortening payables for chip supply [5]. Debtor Days stretched from 24 (FY25) to 46.1 (FY26), and receivables hit ₹212.16 Cr in Sep 2026 [1, 5]. Screens also flag potential interest capitalization on CWIP (₹62.53 Cr in Sep 2026). India Ratings upgraded debt to IND A/Stable (IND A1), but verify Ind AS 23 footnotes for true interest cover [1].

web_blocks.caption: SEDEMAC Cash Flow & Free Cash Flow Conversion (Mar 2021 – Mar 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: FY26 CFO rose to ₹128 Cr (71% pre-tax CFO/EBITDA, -₹47 Cr FCF), but H1 FY27 CFO swung negative to -₹20.38 Cr (vs +₹120.73 Cr YoY) on ₹178 Cr of receivable and inventory build [1].

web_blocks.caption: SEDEMAC Working Capital Cycle & Return Ratios (Mar 2021 – Mar 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: ROCE expanded steadily from 6% (FY22) to 35.3% (FY26), though Debtor Days stretched to 46 days and H1 FY27 debt/capex will test capital efficiency [1].

web_blocks.title: Forensic Checklist: Four Accounting & Cash Items to Monitor in FY27
paragraphs: 1. Short-Term Debt Surge (₹245.64 Cr Debt + ₹106.47 Cr Leases): Current debt jumped 7.4x to ₹153.19 Cr in H1 FY27. Watch if it unwinds in H2 FY27 as MF3 ramps [1, 5].
2. Interest Capitalization & Q2 Interest Step-Up: Quarterly finance cost hit ₹6 Cr in Q2 FY27. Verify how much MF3/MF5 interest was capitalized to CWIP (₹62.53 Cr) under Ind AS 23 [1].
3. Negative H1 CFO (-₹20.38 Cr): Receivables (₹212.16 Cr) and inventory (₹287.81 Cr) drained cash in H1 FY27. H2 FY27 must deliver a sharp positive CFO reversal [1, 5].

4. H1 FY27 Effective Tax-Rate Collapse (19%–22% vs 31% FY26): Screener's quarterly effective tax rate dropped from 43%/33% (Q1/Q2 FY26) to 19%/22% (Q1/Q2 FY27) on the new-regime transition, flattering Q2 PAT (+30.0% YoY) over Q2 PBT (+13.3% YoY) and H1 PAT (+53.2%) over H1 PBT (+22.7%). Track PBT growth closely as the tax rate normalizes toward ~25.17%–30.0% [1, 39].

book_paragraphs: Now let us open the forensic ledger and examine whether SEDEMAC's earnings are backed by clean cash and a fortress balance sheet—or whether rapid growth is starting to strain the plumbing. Look first at the six-year income statement: sales climbed from ₹240 crore in FY21 to ₹1,058 crore in FY26 and ₹1,265 crore on a trailing twelve-month basis, while net profit compounded at 69.4% annually over five years to ₹104 crore in FY26 and ₹129 crore TTM. Return on Capital Employed marched steadily higher from 6% in FY22 to 35.3% in FY26, with Return on Equity at 26.9%. Yet look one line above net profit before celebrating H1 FY27's headline earnings: Screener's quarterly effective tax rate dropped sharply from 43% in Q1 FY26 and 33% in Q2 FY26 (31% for full-year FY26) down to 19% in Q1 FY27 and 22% in Q2 FY27 after SEDEMAC shifted to India's new corporate tax regime. That lower tax bill flattered Q2 FY27 PAT growth (+30.0% YoY, ₹30 crore to ₹39 crore) over underlying Q2 PBT growth (+13.3% YoY, ₹45 crore to ₹51 crore), and lifted H1 FY27 PAT growth (+53.2%, ₹47 crore to ₹72 crore) well ahead of H1 PBT growth (+22.7%, ₹75 crore to ₹92 crore). Once the effective tax rate settles back toward the statutory 25.17%–30.0% zone alongside higher depreciation and finance costs, reported EPS growth will track pre-tax momentum much more closely.

Now turn the page to the September 2026 balance sheet and footnote disclosures, because a dramatic shift happened in just six months between March 2026 and September 2026. On the headline screen, aggregated Borrowings jumped nearly fivefold from ₹72 crore to ₹352 crore, and Fixed Assets more than doubled from ₹253 crore to ₹518 crore. Digging into the footnotes separates the two distinct pieces of that ₹352 crore jump: actual interest-bearing financial borrowings rose from ₹50.63 crore to ₹245.64 crore—with short-term working-capital borrowings surging more than sevenfold from ₹20.75 crore to ₹153.19 crore—while Ind AS 116 lease liabilities climbed to ₹106.47 crore, matched by ₹144.16 crore of Right-of-Use assets for the new MF3 Chakan facility. Quarterly interest expense stepped up from ₹1–2 crore to ₹6 crore in Q2 FY27.

Why did debt and working capital swell so sharply in half a year? First, remember that SEDEMAC's March 2026 IPO was a 100% Offer for Sale—not a single rupee of primary equity entered the company's treasury—so equipping MF3 in Chakan and acquiring 13 acres for MF5 in Tamil Nadu had to be funded with internal accruals, leases, and bank debt. Second, tight global semiconductor lead times forced SEDEMAC to front-load chip inventory (which jumped 52.8% from ₹188.31 crore to ₹287.81 crore) while trade receivables expanded 58.7% from ₹133.72 crore to ₹212.16 crore and management shortened supplier payables.

That working-capital squeeze shows up unmistakably on the H1 FY27 cash flow statement: Operating Cash Flow actually flipped negative to -₹20.38 crore in H1 FY27, compared with positive ₹120.73 crore in H1 FY26. Add in FY26's negative ₹47 crore Free Cash Flow, Debtor Days stretching from 24 days to 46.1 days, and ₹62.53 crore sitting in CWIP with automated screens flagging potential Ind AS 23 interest capitalization, and you have a clear forensic watchlist. India Ratings' upgrade of SEDEMAC's bank facilities to IND A/Stable (short-term IND A1) confirms that lenders remain comfortable with financial debt of ₹245.64 crore against ~₹246 crore of TTM EBITDA (~1.0x financial debt, or ~1.4x including leases)—provided H2 FY27 operating cash flow snaps back strongly into positive territory.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The September 2026 balance sheet marks SEDEMAC's transition from an asset-light, self-funding R&D scale-up into a heavy-capex, debt-assisted manufacturing expansion. A 1.4x total debt-and-lease-to-TTM-EBITDA ratio is manageable, but H1 FY27's negative ₹20.38 crore operating cash flow and 7.4x jump in short-term borrowings remove the margin of safety if semiconductor inflation or OEM demand hiccups hit simultaneously.

book_subsections.title: Stress-Testing Cash Conversion and Interest Capitalization
paragraphs: Let us run one more forensic check on SEDEMAC's cash-conversion cycle so nothing surprises you in future filings. Between FY23 and FY25, SEDEMAC looked almost self-funding: pre-tax CFO-to-EBITDA conversion ran at 166% in FY23, 85% in FY24, and 87% in FY25, and borrowings fell from ₹170 crore in FY24 to ₹64 crore in FY25. In FY26, however, pre-tax CFO-to-EBITDA stepped down to 71% (₹128 crore of CFO on ₹217 crore of EBITDA) as Debtor Days stretched from 24 to 46.1 days, even though Days Payable temporarily ballooned from 76 to 128 days to cushion the working-capital hit.

Then came H1 FY27, when semiconductor tightness forced SEDEMAC to reverse that payable cushion while receivables climbed ₹78.44 crore to ₹212.16 crore and inventories climbed ₹99.50 crore to ₹287.81 crore—flipping H1 operating cash flow to negative ₹20.38 crore (versus +₹120.73 crore a year earlier) and driving short-term borrowings up from ₹20.75 crore to ₹153.19 crore. Over the next four quarters, watch two items like a hawk: first, whether Q2 FY27's ₹6 crore quarterly interest run-rate stays contained alongside Ind AS 23 capitalized interest on CWIP (₹62.53 crore); and second, whether H2 FY27 Operating Cash Flow swings decisively back into positive territory as MF3 commercial production scales.
